page: Amazon Web Services c7gn.xlarge is a compute-optimized server powered by the custom AWS Graviton Neoverse-V1 processor. Built on the arm64 architecture, it features 4 dedicated physical cores running at 2.6 GHz with a single thread per core. The processor is equipped with 64 KB L1d cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache, and 32 MB L3 cache. The instance is provisioned with 8.0 GB of system memory, yielding a memory-to-core ratio of 2.0 GB per core. It operates on the AWS Nitro hypervisor and does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware.

Benchmark results show average performance across several standard compute and memory tasks. The server achieved a stress-ng single-core score of 1532.39 and a multi-core score of 6112.46. Memory bandwidth is notable, with read-only cached small block speeds reaching 386.35 GB/sec and uncached large block write speeds at 39.43 GB/sec. However, cryptographic and complex instruction workloads show limitations, as evidenced by a poor rating in the Passmark CPU encryption test of 550.39 and weak ratings in Passmark CPU extended instructions. Multi-threaded bzip3 decompression and ray tracing benchmarks also fell into the weak performance tier.

The c7gn.xlarge is network and EBS optimized, delivering a baseline network bandwidth of 12 Gbps. From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the ARM-based architecture provides a balanced compute-to-memory profile for workloads that do not require x86 instruction sets. This makes it suitable for network-intensive applications, static web serving, Redis key-value stores, and software compilation. It is less suited for heavy cryptographic processing or large-scale LLM inference.
description: Amazon Web Services c7gn.xlarge is an arm64 compute-optimized server running on the AWS Nitro hypervisor. It features 4 dedicated physical cores powered by an AWS Graviton Neoverse-V1 processor at 2.6 GHz, paired with 8.0 GB of memory. The instance lacks local storage and dedicated GPUs but provides a baseline network bandwidth of 12 Gbps. Performance benchmarks indicate average capabilities in general integer and memory operations, with a stress-ng multi-core score of 6112.46 and static web serving throughput of 8.15 GB/sec. However, it exhibits weaker performance in cryptographic and extended instruction tests. This server is qualitatively cost-efficient for network-optimized, ARM-compatible workloads such as static web serving, software compilation, and Redis database operations, while being less suited for intensive cryptographic tasks or large language model inference.
